title: Longest Fibonacci Subarray
summary: Given an array of positive integers, identify the longest contiguous subarray where each element (starting from the third) is the sum of the two preceding elements, adhering to the Fibonacci sequence rule.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, identify the longest contiguous subarray where each element (starting from the third) is the sum of the two preceding elements, adhering to the Fibonacci sequence rule. Note that any subarray of length 1 or 2 is considered Fibonacci.
constraints: nums contains three to 100,000 positive integers.
A contiguous subarray is Fibonacci when every element from the third onward equals the previous two summed.
Length-one and length-two subarrays always qualify.
hints: A failed equality ends only the longer run; its final two values can begin the next candidate.
Scan once while storing the length of the Fibonacci run ending at the current index.
Extend on a valid sum and otherwise reset the run length to two.
The state is exactly the longest valid subarray ending at each position, so its maximum is the global answer.
editorial: The state is exactly the longest valid subarray ending at each position, so its maximum is the global answer.

tests.explanation: Every element from the third onward is the sum of its predecessors, so the answer is five.
